mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in workplace attendance, as observed over the last four weeks, directly translates to increased foot traffic in retail and recreation areas during weekdays, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: When transit station activity recovers by more than 2 percentage points week-on-week, it indicates a broader return to pre-pandemic commuting and leisure travel patterns, boosting retail and recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 14 days even when TRANSIT shows a week-on-week rise exceeding 2 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decrease in residential time and an increase in workplace attendance indicates a strong shift away from home-bound activities, freeing up time for discretionary retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days despite both RESIDENTIAL decreasing and WORKPLACES increasing.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of seasonal transition towards potentially less favorable outdoor weather, a decline in parks activity suggests a shift from outdoor leisure to indoor retail and recreation, leading to higher RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC decreases over the next 7 days while PARKS continues to decline, indicating no shift to indoor retail.

mechanism_narrative: The recent upward trend in RETAIL_REC mobility, observed over the last week (t-1w to t-0w), indicates a momentum that will likely continue, driving further recovery in the short term over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its value at t-0w, breaking the recent upward momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in grocery and pharmacy visits, exceeding 1 percentage point week-on-week, suggests reduced essential errands, freeing up time and budget for discretionary retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by more than 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next 14 days despite GROCERY_PHARM falling by more than 1 percentage point week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: An increasing trend in transit usage coupled with a decreasing trend in parks visits suggests a shift from outdoor, potentially local, leisure activities to more structured, transit-dependent retail and recreation destinations over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, even with TRANSIT increasing and PARKS decreasing.

mechanism_narrative: In a period of sustained reopening, a continued decline in residential mobility indicates people are spending less time at home, which directly correlates with increased out-of-home activities including retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases despite RESIDENTIAL mobility continuing its downward trend.
